sections.text:
In a small, quiet French village, there lived a very beautiful girl who was different from the rest of the girls in her village, called “Belle” (the beautiful one).

While the other girls were fussing over dresses and parties, Belle spent all her time reading books with great passion.

She always dreamed of adventures and romantic stories that she read about, and wished to live a life full of excitement far away from her boring village.

Belle lived with her father, Maurice, an eccentric but kind-hearted inventor who loved his daughter more than anything in the world.

One cold winter day, Morris set out on a trip to display his latest invention at an exhibition in the city.

While traveling through the dark forest, Maurice lost his way due to a strong blizzard and heard the sounds of hungry wolves chasing him.

His horse ran terrified, and Maurice found himself in front of the huge iron gates of an abandoned and terrifying castle, so he entered them to take shelter from the cold and the wolves.

The castle was strangely enchanted; The furniture moves and talks, such as the clock, the candlestick, the teapot, and the small teacup.

They welcomed him and offered him warmth and food, but before he left in the morning, Maurice remembered his promise to his daughter Belle that he would bring her a rose.

He picked a beautiful red rose from the castle garden, and at that very moment, the owner of the castle appeared, a huge and very frightening “monster.”

The Beast was so angry that Maurice stole his rose after hosting him, he decided to imprison him in the cold tower of the castle forever.

Maurice's horse returned alone to the village, so Belle knew that her father was in danger, and she rode the horse that led her to the cursed castle.

Belle sneaked in and found her father sick in the cell, and when the monster appeared, she begged him to release her sick old father.

Belle bravely suggested that she remain a prisoner in the castle in her father's place, and although the father was sad, the Beast agreed to this exchange and forced the father to leave.

In the early days, Belle was terrified by the monster's appearance and his angry, terrifying voice, and refused to have dinner with him.

But the castle's magical servants (the candlestick and the teapot) tried to comfort her, and arranged for her a wonderful dinner and a cheerful musical parade.

As time passed, Belle began to discover that beneath this terrifying appearance of a monster, hidden a kind heart, a noble soul, and an educated personality.

The monster allowed her to enter his huge library, which included thousands of books, and that was the most beautiful gift she could receive.

They began spending a lot of time together, reading, talking, and taking walks in the snow-covered castle gardens.

The secret that Belle did not know was that the Beast was originally a handsome and arrogant prince, who was punished by an evil witch by turning him into a beast because he refused to host her on a cold night.

The witch's spell said: He will remain a monster until he falls in love with a woman, and she reciprocates his true love before the last petal of a magical red rose falls.

One evening, while they were dancing together in the magnificent palace hall, the Beast asked Belle if she was happy with him.

Belle replied that she was happy, but that she missed her father very much and wished she could check on him, so the monster gave her a magic mirror to see her father.

Belle saw her father very sick in the forest searching for her, so the monster begged her to go save him, even though he knew that the time of the curse was coming to an end.

Belle returned to the village and rescued her father, but the evil villagers, led by an arrogant person named Gaston, incited the people to attack the castle and kill the monster.

Belle rushed back to save the monster, arriving to find the monster lying on the edge of the roof, badly injured after his fight with Gaston, who had fallen to his death.

Belle cried bitterly, hugged the monster who was breathing his last, and said sincerely: “Don’t leave me, I love you!”

At that very moment, before the last petal of the magical rose fell, a great miracle happened.

The sky glowed, the wounds began to disappear, and the terrifying monster transformed into a very handsome prince and returned to his human nature.

The castle returned to life, the magical servants turned into humans again, Belle married the prince, and they lived in true happiness that did not depend on appearances.
